mechanism: RSI (Wilder: RS=avg_up/avg_down, RSI=100-100/(1+RS)) occupies different bands by market regime: uptrend mostly mid-to-70, downtrend mid-to-30, sideways between 30–70. Trade rules are regime-gated (up: RSI<50 buy / >70 TP; down: RSI>50 short / <30 TP; sideways: <30 buy / >70 short with mid exits). Also notes divergence and failure swings above 70 / below 30 as reversal warnings.
data_needed: Close series; RSI period (default 14); prior regime label (up/down/sideways); optional price–RSI divergence check
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iRSI; educational OHLC table; no fixed instrument
why_new_for_mis: Frames RSI not as a universal OB/OS switch but as a regime-conditioned momentum-band occupancy sensor whose thresholds flip with trend vs range.
quote: In this case, most of the time RSI values move between or moving between the mid range and level 70 (Overbought level).

mechanism: MT5 Momentum = (Close_t/Close_{t-n})*100 oscillates about 100. Cross above 100 = buy (gated to uptrend only); cross below 100 = short (gated to downtrend). Author flags early signals and whipsaws in sideways and prefers other tools there—so the 100-line is a velocity-change sensor that needs an external regime filter.
data_needed: Close series; Momentum period n=14; external trend/regime label
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iMomentum; illustrative 15-day close table
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a simple price-velocity ratio sensor around a fixed null (100) plus an explicit caveat that sideways regimes invalidate it.
quote: When Momentum line breaks 100 upwards, it will be a buy signal. When Momentum line breaks 100 downwards, it will be a short signal.

mechanism: CCI=(TP−SMA(TP))/(0.015·MeanDeviation) measures how far typical price sits from its mean in mean-deviation units. Regime-gated: uptrend CCI>100 buy; downtrend CCI<−100 short; sideways mean-revert at ±100; alternate zero-line cross entries with ±100 TP.
data_needed: High/Low/Close (TP); CCI period 14; regime label; ±100 and 0 thresholds
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a calibrated mean-deviation excursion oscillator whose ±100 / zero levels are interpreted differently under trend vs sideways regimes.
quote: when CCI is high this means that the prices are far above its average and vice versa, when CCI is low this means that the prices are far below its average.

mechanism: Limit-order grid is preferred when price oscillates in a declared flat range (e.g. VBM2 1600–2800 RUB); boundary break ≈ flat end / new trend. Optionally size equidistant grid step from ATR percentage on D1 so spacing exceeds spread yet matches typical daily range. Range membership + ATR% step jointly gate whether the mean-reverting grid is appropriate.
data_needed: User HIGH/LOW price bounds; Number_of_elements_in_the_grid; D1 ATR (or ATR%); symbol spread; MOEX contract specs/margin
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MOEX futures VTBR-6.22 (VBM2); example range RUB 1600–2800, 10 grid elements; ATR on D1 mentioned; ~1-month narrative
why_new_for_mis: Treats explicit price-range membership plus ATR%-scaled spacing as a flat-vs-trend suitability sensor for range-harvesting systems.
quote: The most preferable flat type for grid trading is the one when the price moves in a certain range without a clearly defined direction. The breakdown of the boundaries, as a rule, means the end of the flat and the beginning of a new trend.

mechanism: Stop-order (BuyStop/SellStop) grid step chosen from a few pips above spread up to average daily true range via ATR; smaller step = more aggressive. Wide flat channels can fire many stops both ways and create deep drawdowns—so ATR-scaled step plus detection of wide two-sided stop activation acts as a volatility/structure risk sensor for trend-grid systems.
data_needed: ATR (period matching horizon); grid width/step in points; count of simultaneous opposite stop fills; MOEX margin per contract
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MOEX Sberbank futures SBRF-6.23; VTB ordinary-share futures; example grid width 3500 pts, step 184, TP 100; ATR for step sizing
why_new_for_mis: Links ATR-based spacing to a concrete failure mode (wide-flat multi-stop activation) usable as a MIS risk/regime veto for stop-grids.
quote: This value can be determined by the Average True Range (ATR) indicator, which shows how much the price of a symbol has changed over a certain period of time (a measure of volatility).

mechanism: MACD line = EMA12−EMA26; Signal = EMA9(MACD). Zero-line side of the MACD main line defines setup: MACD>0 → bullish/buy setup; MACD<0 → bearish/short setup. Separate sensor: MACD vs Signal crossover for entry timing within that setup.
data_needed: Close series; MACD params 12,26,9; main and signal buffers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iMACD; 34-period worked EMA example
why_new_for_mis: Separates a persistent bull/bear setup bit (zero-line regime) from the faster line-crossover timing signal—clean two-layer MACD sensing for MIS.
quote: If the MACD main line breaks above zero level, this will be a buying setup or bullish setup and vice versa if MACD main line breaks below zero level, this will be a shorting setup or bearish.

mechanism: %K=100*(Close−LL)/(HH−LL) over N (fast/slow variants with %D MA). Empirical regime fingerprint: uptrend Stoch mostly 50–100; downtrend 0–50; sideways ~20–80. Entries are regime-gated crossovers (%K/%D cross below 50 in uptrend; above 50 in downtrend; OB/OS 80/20 in sideways).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iStochastic; 20-day HH/LL worked example
why_new_for_mis: Uses close-location-in-range as a regime fingerprint and gates %K/%D crosses by that band—MIS can treat Stoch band occupancy as a soft regime prior.
quote: we can find during this market direction that most of the time, closing prices tend to close near the upper part of range price during that period of movement "Uptrend" and the stochastic indicator will oscillate between 50 level and 100 level.

mechanism: From +DM/−DM and TR build +DI/−DI and DX; ADX=avg(DX). Current ADX>previous ⇒ ADX rising (trend present); ADX falling ⇒ no trend. Directional trades when ADX>25 and rising: +DI>−DI buy; +DI<−DI sell. Separates trend-presence from trend-direction.
data_needed: High/Low/Close; ADX period 14; ADX,+DI,−DI buffers; threshold 25
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iADX; 30-day DM/TR worked example
why_new_for_mis: Classic but explicit three-state sensing: trend-on (ADX rising &>25) vs trend-off, then +DI/−DI for signed direction—core MIS regime stack.
quote: if the ADX curve is moving up, this means that there is a trend and vice versa if the ADX curve is moving down, this means that there is no trend.

mechanism: TR=max(H−L,|H−prevC|,|L−prevC|); ATR=avg(TR,14). ATR measures magnitude only (rising ATR ≠ uptrend). Sensors: (1) strength vs instrument-specific thresholds (e.g. EURUSD >0.0024 strong / <0.0014 weak); (2) ATR_t ≷ ATR_{t−1} ⇒ volatility expanding/contracting; (3) dynamic SL/TP = ±2×ATR and ±4×ATR from bid/ask.
data_needed: High/Low/Close; ATR period 14; calibrated strong/weak cutoffs per symbol/TF; Ask/Bid for SL/TP
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD Mar–Apr 2022 daily TR/ATR example; ATR on H1 chart; generic iATR(_Symbol,_Period,14)
why_new_for_mis: Pure volatility amplitude + expansion/contraction sensors plus ATR-multiple risk geometry, explicitly decoupled from price direction.
quote: ATR does not provide price or market direction but it provides only the volatility measurement.

mechanism: Rising SAR = priorSAR + priorAF*(priorEP−priorSAR); falling SAR subtracts; AF steps 0.02→0.20 on new EP. SAR below prior low ⇒ buy / trail; SAR above prior high ⇒ sell / trail or TP on flip. Stop is function of both time (moves every bar) and price (tracks EP)—stop-and-reverse regime flip sensor.
data_needed: High/Low; iSAR step=0.02 max=0.2; prior bar high/low for flip tests
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iSAR; rising/falling SAR worked tables
why_new_for_mis: Provides a time-and-price trailing-stop level whose flip across price is an explicit stop-and-reverse / regime-change event for MIS.
quote: the main objective of this Parabolic SAR indicator is to create trailing stops. The stop is a function of two things: time and price

mechanism: OBV accumulates signed tick/contract volume (add on up-close, subtract on down-close, flat if unchanged). Sensors: OBV_t≷OBV_{t−1} rising/declining flow; OBV vs avg of prior 4 OBV for strong/weak; during uptrend OBV↑ and HH ⇒ strong up move; during downtrend OBV↓ and LL ⇒ strong down move—volume-confirms-price participation sensing.
data_needed: Close + VOLUME_TICK (or real volume); OBV series; prior highs/lows; 4-bar OBV average
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol/_Period via iOBV(...,VOLUME_TICK); illustrative close/volume table
why_new_for_mis: Turns signed volume accumulation into flow-direction, relative-strength, and price-volume confirmation sensors for MIS liquidity/participation.
quote: It measures the positive and negative volume flow.
